components.evidence: PE32/PE32+ mapping, relocations and normal imports are tested. Exports, name/ordinal lookup, forwarded exports with bounded depth and cycle detection, runtime-to-runtime import binding, and the PE32 TLS directory plus a process/thread TLS owner with callback plans are implemented and host-tested; delay imports remain.
Wine modules have an explicit runtime origin; POSIX and PS5 providers keep independently configured application/runtime roots, covered by host tests.

The first PE32 title is playable on FW 12.02 with exact host parity and bounded hardware evidence. For Wine, the translator now also covers FS-prefixed absolute dword operands, LOCK-prefixed group-1 memory read-modify-write, BT/BTS/BTR/BTC, CMOVcc, the SSE data-movement/lane slice (movd/movq/movdqa/movdqu/movups/movaps/movss/movsd, punpck/packss, pshufd and friends, pextrw/pinsrw), BSF/BSR and the 16-bit shift group, each with architectural tests and residency/lazy-flag parity where the form allows it. With the Unix-call bridge enabled, real ntdll initialization runs 8582 instructions, services three NtAllocateVirtualMemory calls and maps 88 KiB of guest memory before it needs a populated process environment (CurrentDirectory.Buffer is null in the gate's zeroed process-parameters page).
Synthetic integer call bridge exists; imports, callbacks, FP/vector arguments and exception transitions remain.

The pinned revision 490f6d5d builds a reproducible i386 PE runtime (recorded in a validated manifest; the reproducibility claim is two forced rebuilds in one pinned build tree) and a bounded host gate maps it from PW_FILE_RUNTIME, binds kernelbase's 428 imports against ntdll's exports, services the first Unix calls behind a versioned table and executes real ntdll initialization: with the bridge enabled the run retires 32 544 instructions, services three NtAllocateVirtualMemory calls, opens the Windows directory, queries its FileFsDeviceInformation, releases the process-parameters block ntdll replaces during init_user_process_params, answers the Wine version class, opens the Session Manager registry key and reads its options, answers the process token's user SID, opens the user hive root with NtCreateKey, reads the version-init registry keys, opens the \KnownDlls directory object, looks for a section in it, reaches the boundary through Wine's second stub shape (mov eax, id; call fs:[0xc0], the dispatcher the unix side publishes in TEB.WOW32Reserved), describes the process image out of the mapped module's own PE headers, and then stops with returned-to-caller at 0 because the loader's own debug message calls __wine_unix_call_dispatcher, the second dispatcher the gate does not publish yet. The gate also builds a minimal populated RTL_USER_PROCESS_PARAMETERS (current directory, DLL and image paths, command line, environment). No Windows process starts yet and no title uses it: the unix-call surface, NLS, threads and the rest of the loader remain.

The dispatcher boundary is located in the built image (exported __wine_syscall_dispatcher slot plus the single jmp-dword-ptr thunk that references it) and the call number is re-read from the issuing stub inside the mapped image; both stub shapes Wine's build emits are bridged, the 'mov edx, <thunk>' form and the 'call fs:[0xc0]' form whose target is the dispatcher the gate publishes in TEB.WOW32Reserved exactly as Wine's unix side does. A versioned table of the pinned i386 syscall numbers, names and argument widths is cross-checked against the Wine source - all 256 i386 entries - and the two-level stub frame is unwound correctly. Sixteen unique call handlers are implemented - fifteen in the dispatch registry plus the classified NtTerminateProcess stop - and the dynamic run services 19 calls through the registry: NtAllocateVirtualMemory, NtFreeVirtualMemory (whole-region MEM_RELEASE only), NtOpenFile, NtReadFile, NtQueryInformationFile, NtQueryVolumeInformationFile (FileFsDeviceInformation), NtOpenKey, NtCreateKey (create-or-open against the profile), NtQueryValueKey, NtQuerySystemInformation (the Wine version class), NtQueryInformationToken (TokenUser), NtOpenDirectoryObject, NtOpenSection, NtQueryInformationProcess (ProcessImageInformation), NtTerminateProcess (current process, a classified stop) and NtClose. The two VM calls preflight every output span before they reserve, commit, release or account anything, and their backend failures are injected and asserted, so those two commit completely or not at all. The run now stops with returned-to-caller at 0 because the loader's debug output calls __wine_unix_call_dispatcher, the second dispatcher this bridge does not publish yet. The bridge is split the way it is used: src/pw_wine_gate.c orchestrates the run and owns the virtual-memory calls, and the adapters are units with their own contracts - src/pw_wine_path.c (guest names turned into canonical strings for all three namespaces), src/pw_wine_handle.c (the run's side of the typed handle table), src/pw_wine_file.c, src/pw_wine_registry.c, src/pw_wine_object.c and src/pw_wine_query.c - each behind its own platform service or, for the queries, answering from host state. Remaining: the unix-call surface, the reserve/commit distinction, threads and NLS, and the same rollback guarantee for the handlers that are not the two VM calls.

One guest thread has isolated CPU/FP/FS state. PE32 TLS now has a process/thread owner: stable module indices published through mapped guest memory, per-thread template-plus-zero-fill storage from a caller-owned arena, guest FS:[0x2C] lookup and deterministic attach/detach callback plans driven by the DBT's guest-callback mechanism, with two-thread and rollback coverage. The Wine gate additionally owns a minimal guest TEB (FS base, StackBase, StackLimit, Self, ProcessEnvironmentBlock) and a zeroed PEB so real ntdll initialization can run. Real PEB/PEB_LDR_DATA construction, module entry-point ordering and native thread adapters remain.
No general Wine-compatible object/handle or WaitForMultipleObjects service is claimed.
Low-address reserve/commit/protect/release and W^X DBT publication are validated for the current profile.
Precise DBT faults exist, but PE32 SEH dispatch/unwind and Wine context delivery do not.

Title-confined read/seek and INI access exist. For Wine, the Unix-call bridge now has a bounded file service: NtOpenFile, NtReadFile, NtQueryInformationFile (FileStandardInformation), NtQueryVolumeInformationFile (FileFsDeviceInformation) and NtClose are serviced behind a gate-owned handle table, with every guest pointer validated through the dispatcher's accessor and a path translation that accepts only single components under C:\windows\system32 or C:\windows, so traversal is refused before the platform is consulted. The same handle table now carries registry keys (NtOpenKey, NtCreateKey, NtQueryValueKey against a host-supplied registry profile, absolute and relative, with a validated \Registry\Machine / \Registry\User namespace) and object-namespace directories and sections (NtOpenDirectoryObject, NtOpenSection against an object profile that declares \KnownDlls and no sections, so the loader falls back to the file system the way it does on a prefix without known DLLs). The host side is a pluggable service, so the portable core still makes no file-system call and holds no registry or object content. The loader's first open is the Windows directory itself, which the gate answers as a gate-owned directory object with Directory = 1; a Wine prefix registry and object namespace, broader NT path semantics, sharing, directory enumeration and overlapped I/O remain.
A bounded persistent registry and CP1252 bootstrap exist; Wine registry views, environment and Unicode/NLS remain.
WinMM PCM and DualSense-to-message adapters are hardware validated for one title.
No Winsock compatibility surface is claimed.
DXVK is the selected D3D8/9/10/11 path; it has not started on PS5.
The companion project renders and computes on gfx1013 but does not yet satisfy its pinned DXVK consumer profile.
ps5log/1 identity, runtime counters and ordered close/relaunch are hardware validated.
